title: Installer dependency auto-provisioning — WIZARD.md Step 0 comprehension
method: Fresh agent given ONLY the Step 0 section, no other context. Answers must come from the text alone. Correct = instructions are unambiguous; wrong = implementation/clarity gap → reject.

questions.q: During prerequisite detection, the very first missing dependency is found. Should the installer stop and report it immediately, or keep checking the rest?
questions.expected: Keep checking / do NOT bail on the first — gather-all enumerates all missing deps in one pass; never fail-fast.

questions.q: When deps are missing, how many permission/consent questions does the user get before anything is installed?
questions.expected: Exactly one consent question for the full missing-set; install nothing before the user answers.

questions.q: The user DECLINES provisioning, and the ONLY missing item is the `claude` CLI. Does the install hard-stop?
questions.expected: No — claude is soft; note the install could still proceed (agent spawn would be unavailable) and let the user reconsider; not a hard blocker.

questions.q: After re-verify, a hard dependency (gh / Python / pip / packages) is STILL missing. What does the installer do?
questions.expected: Show the still-missing items + instruct lines, tell the user what to install, exit cleanly with code 0 (no repo writes happened, nothing to roll back); user fixes env and re-runs.

questions.q: Does Phase 0 provisioning write anything to the target repository?
questions.expected: No — it installs host tools / Python packages only (consent-gated); no writes to the target repo. Aborting leaves nothing changed.

questions.q: After the user approves, what exact command provisions all the auto-provisionable items?
questions.expected: `python references/scripts/wizard.py provision-deps` (no args = provision every auto item).
